title: spec review: S2d1 cache-aware context router in shadow: cacheability, effective cache cost and a cache-adjusted level per evidence item on context_selection rows (P8)
spec:
orchestrator/context_router.py: for every routed evidence item compute cacheability (stable for repo files at a pinned commit, semi for memory, dynamic for tool outputs, test results and worker_partial) and cache_cost = cache_telemetry.dynamic_cost(chars, provider, cfg), a new small read-only helper in orchestrator/cache_telemetry.py (scope) that applies the [cache] ratios of effective_cost to a char count (chars/4 tokens) and returns None when the [cache] section or telemetry ratios are missing. Shadow algorithm for cache_adjusted_level, defined exactly: start from the presented level; downgrade one step (FULL to LONG, LONG to SHORT) when cacheability is dynamic and cache_cost exceeds [context_router].cache_downgrade_tokens (default 600); upgrade one step (SHORT to LONG) when cacheability is stable and cache_cost is below [context_router].cache_upgrade_tokens (default 200); never change an item whose level came from a hard-constraint FULL reason (in_scope_file, security_path, failing_output, acceptance); HIDE items stay HIDE. Rows: the existing kind context_selection keeps its candidates shape; the deterministic dict gains three parallel maps keyed by evidence id: cacheability, cache_cost, cache_adjusted_level, plus cache_data = ok|missing. Presented levels never change unless [context_router].cache_mode is active (add cache_mode = "shadow" with a dated comment and revert instruction to [context_router]; missing key means off; unknown values raise at config load in pool validation; cache_mode is inert whenever the section's mode is off; tests/test_pool.py covers the validation and the gating). Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/10-cache-aware-disclosure.md section 1 with the algorithm and a reproducible command (`orchestrator scorecard --context --cache-shadow`, added to the context scorecard output, scope orchestrator/cli.py) that prints, over the decision_log rows present, the row count, date range and the share of items whose cache_adjusted_level differs from the presented level; when no rows exist the doc says so.
Spec review T-1246 folded in: (1) Validation lives in context_router.cache_mode(cfg) (returns off|shadow|active, raises ValueError on anything else; missing key is off); pool.py and tests/test_pool.py leave the scope; the validation test lives in tests/test_context_router.py. (2) Authoritative mode: spawn._context_mode's effective mode (which already downgrades active to shadow when the context eval is missing or stale) is passed into route(..., effective_mode=) by spawn.py (scope adds orchestrator/spawn.py and tests/test_spawn.py); cache_mode active applies adjusted levels only when effective_mode is active. (3) Cacheability table, explicit: stable = source_chunk, architecture_note, decision, memory_entry whose commit equals the head_sha given to route() ('pinned'); semi = scout_finding, graph_finding, review_finding, previous_result, external_doc, and any stable type whose commit differs from head_sha; dynamic = test_result and any item whose provenance is worker_partial. (4) cache_cost input: the chars of _text(ev, presented_level) (the tokens_at_level quantity), provider passed as route(..., provider=) by spawn (codex for a Codex dispatch, claude otherwise); provider None yields cache_cost None and cache_data missing. (5) Algorithm corrected: no FULL-to-LONG step (FULL only comes from hard constraints); downgrade LONG-to-SHORT only for dynamic items whose reason is not in the exempt set {hard-constraint FULL reasons, skill_required_context, read_scope, section_items}; upgrade SHORT-to-LONG only for stable items whose reason is the generic source_type fallback. (6) Plumbing: the Routed dataclass gains optional fields cacheability, cache_cost, cache_adjusted_level (default None) and RoutedPacket exposes them; decision_row writes the three parallel maps into the deterministic dict; the candidates list keeps its exact shape in shadow (a test asserts byte-identical candidates with and without cache_mode); in active mode the presented level itself changes so the candidates suffixes follow, and tokens_at_level is computed from the adjusted level.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_context_router.py::test_cache_fields_on_rows_and_presented_level_unchanged_in_shadow (route() levels identical with cache_mode shadow and with no cache_mode key; deterministic maps present)
tests/test_context_router.py::test_cache_adjusted_level_algorithm (downgrade, upgrade, hard-constraint FULL untouched, HIDE untouched, missing telemetry gives None and cache_data missing)

risks.issue: Upgrade rule (5) contradicts the exempt set. The only reason a stable SHORT item gets from the generic source_type fallback is 'read_scope' (line 93, source_chunk SHORT). 'read_scope' is also in the downgrade exempt set and is forced to SHORT by section_items (line 152). The upgrade therefore either never fires or fires on items whose SHORT is deliberate. The planner role also returns 'read_scope' for source_chunk (line 72). The spec must name the exact reason strings and roles the upgrade applies to. It must also say what happens to section_items, which overrides the level for the read_scope section.

dynamic_cost is under-specified. It must return None when [cache] or the ratios are missing, but _cache_cfg (line 29) silently merges DEFAULT_RATIOS. Reusing it would never return None. The spec does not say which ratio applies to an item: read, write or a mix. effective_cost uses read and write ratios on different buckets, and the provider ratios differ (claude write 1.25, codex write 1.0). Nothing defines cache_cost = f(chars/4, provider). The 600 and 200 thresholds cannot be checked without that formula. 'Telemetry ratios' is also ambiguous: config ratios, or ratios observed from runs.

Validation location and failure path. cache_mode(cfg) raising ValueError inside route() is swallowed by spawn._shadow_route's broad except (line 450). That gives a notify and an empty return, so no decision_log row is written and telemetry is silently lost. 'Raise at config load' is no longer true once pool.py leaves scope. The existing promotion.current_mode instead falls back to the default with an invalid_config flag. The spec should say where cache_mode(cfg) is called at load or spawn time, and what happens on a bad value (fail loudly versus fall back to off).

Cacheability table gaps. 'Commit equals head_sha' applies to memory_entry, but Evidence.commit is often empty for memory items (make() defaults commit=''). Those items are then always semi, and decision and architecture_note are always semi as well. Stable is effectively source_chunk only, and route() may get head_sha=None. The spec does not define behaviour for head_sha None (stale-check-free) or for empty commit. It does not say which rule wins when provenance is worker_partial and source_type is also in the stable list. Dynamic is checked first in the text, but state the precedence.

Downgrading dynamic LONG to SHORT would hit 'prior_worker_overlap' (LONG, worker_partial). That reason is not in the exempt set. Active mode would then shrink prior-worker evidence and change prior_worker_chars in the row extra (spawn.py line 435). It would also bypass the 'unrelated', 'ambiguous' and 'dependency' reasoning for test_result. The spec should either exempt prior_worker_overlap or state the downgrade is intended and test it. Also state that skill_required_context is preserved after adjustment.

suggested_spec_changes: Resolve the upgrade/exempt contradiction: list exact reason strings and roles for the upgrade (for example source_chunk with reason read_scope and role in execute/review/security_review), and remove read_scope from the downgrade exempt set or state that section_items keeps forcing SHORT for that section.

Define cache_cost exactly: tokens = chars // 4; cost = tokens * ratio, naming which ratio (for example {provider}_write_ratio for dynamic and {provider}_read_ratio for stable). dynamic_cost must read only the explicit [cache] table with no DEFAULT_RATIOS merge, and return None when the table or a required key is missing.

Say where cache_mode(cfg) is called and what happens on an invalid value, so it cannot be swallowed by _shadow_route's except. Prefer failing loudly at spawn or at the CLI, or falling back to off with a notify, and test the chosen path.
Specify the stable rule for empty Evidence.commit and head_sha=None, and state dynamic-before-stable precedence.
Exempt prior_worker_overlap from the downgrade, or add a test showing it is intended and that prior_worker_chars is computed from the adjusted level.

Define the decision_log row shape for the CLI summary (fields read, exclusion of rows with cache_data=missing or no cache maps, the denominator, output text and the no-rows message) and where the flag is registered next to --context; require the doc to be generated from those exact strings.
In active mode, log both presented and adjusted levels so the shadow comparison stays measurable, and state which of them the counts, candidates and hard_constraints in the row reflect.
Add rollback: setting cache_mode back to "shadow" or removing the key; note the revert path in the dated comment and in the doc.

Plumbing has two call sites (spawn.py lines 742 and 1055) and _shadow_route computes mode itself. Effective_mode must be threaded via _shadow_route into route(), and provider must be derived from the dispatch (codex or claude) at both sites. In active mode, section_items and render use item.level, and the row's 'hard_constraints' and counts change. The spec should say whether counts and candidates in the row show the presented (adjusted) or original level in active mode. The maps keyed by evidence id are only useful if the pre-adjustment level is also logged. Also, effective_mode 'active' from _context_mode never returns 'off', so the 'inert whenever mode is off' gate lives in spawn returning {} early. Test that path explicitly.

'scorecard --context --cache-shadow' has no defined reader for decision_log rows. It does not say how rows are loaded, which rows count (kind context_selection with a cache_adjusted_level map), how rows without cache fields or with cache_data=missing are excluded from the differing-share denominator, or the output format. The argparse mode table around line 364 uses fixed flag tuples, so adding a flag needs a matching entry there. The acceptance test cannot be checked without an output format and a fixture row shape.

Rollback and defaults. The cache_downgrade_tokens and cache_upgrade_tokens keys are not required in pool.toml, but the spec should say to add them with the same dated-comment style and state their validation (non-negative ints; upgrade < downgrade). The dated comment must be 2026-09-23. Shadow-mode default for cache_mode is set in pool.toml, so it makes every dispatch call dynamic_cost. Specify that dynamic_cost failure cannot abort route().
